To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified 10 proteins that are differentially expressed in patients with abdominal aortic aneursyms compared to healthy controls and that we identified 2 proteins (alpha-2-macroglobulin and complement component C3) that are associated with abdominal aortic diameter.
the plasma proteome of AAA patients was altered compared to controls and that this was associated with an altered inflammatory state.
the proteome of the blood of patients with AAA differs from that of controls, and the differences are associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, and coagulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the proteome of patients with abdominal aortic anaurysm (AAA).
the study of the proteomic profile in the serum of patients with AAA and its correlation with the clinical and morphological parameters of the disease.
the identification of proteins that are associated with abdominal aortic anaurysm (AAA) in the serum of patients with AAA.

there is a lack of evidence to support a role of proteomics in the diagnosis and prognosis of patients with AAA, and that further studies are needed to determine the clinical value of proteomic approaches for this disease.
